# `to dotenv` for [formats](/commands/categories/formats.md)

<div class='command-title'>Convert a record into .env text.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> to dotenv {flags} ```


## Input/output types:

| input  | output |
| ------ | ------ |
| record | string |
## Examples

Write a record as .env text, quoting values that need it.
```nu
> {PORT: 8080, NAME: 'my app', GREETING: "it's"} | to dotenv
PORT=8080
NAME='my app'
GREETING="it's"

```

Round-trip a record through .env text.
```nu
> {URL: 'http://${HOST}/', NOTE: "two\nlines"} | to dotenv | from dotenv
╭──────┬─────────────────╮
│ URL  │ http://${HOST}/ │
│ NOTE │ two             │
│      │ lines           │
╰──────┴─────────────────╯
```

Save a record to a .env file.
```nu
> {PORT: 8080, NAME: 'my app'} | save .env

```

## Notes
Each value is written as an external command would see it, so a `PATH` list is joined with the path separator and the `to_string` conversions in `$env.ENV_CONVERSIONS` apply, and `null` is written as an empty value. A value of plain characters is written bare; any other is single-quoted, or double-quoted with escapes when it holds a `'` or a line break, so `from dotenv` reads back the same text. `save` writes a record to a file named like `.env`, `.env.local` or `prod.env` with this command.
